name: Uel
overview: Uel is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Bani. He is noted specifically for having married a foreign wife, a detail that highlights the post-exilic challenges faced by the returned Israelites in maintaining covenantal purity. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Uel is a proper name that possibly means "will of God" or "will of El," reflecting a theistic element common in Hebrew names. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Uel as a descendant of Bani, establishing a familial link within the post-exilic community. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Uel's mention in Ezra 10:34 is significant as it illustrates the issue of intermarriage with foreign wives among the returned exiles, which was a matter of covenantal concern and reform. His inclusion in the list underscores the communal effort to address and rectify breaches of the law, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness to God's commands in the restoration period.
